items.name: Lou's Engineering Notes
items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.title: Turrets
entries.text:
I've found a store of military-grade turrets in an old observatory to the South. No idea why they needed this firepower. It's mine now.

These turrets are in good shape. I've tested a few, and they all seem to work. I still can't bring myself to walk in front of one, but I have a new plan to work around that...

entries.title: Trial Run #2
entries.text:
The turrets are all set up, but those giant, hideous rats keep running through the room and setting 'em off. Their corpses are...liquidy. Makes my stomach churn, thinking that that will be me.

Tremors have also been a problem. Yeah, tremors. Yesterday I replaced all the turret wiring, and then a small quake set them off. Somehow, they ended up targeting each other. Now I need new turrets.

I'm starting to sour on this whole damned plan.

entries.title: Failure
entries.text:
OK, I'm done here.

Everything was setup perfectly today. Perfectly! I was eating another "last meal" over by the excavator, when a damned rock fell on the button and activated the turrets.

They targeted me, but the excavator blocked most of the fire. Two of the rounds grazed my arm, and god this hurts worse than I thought it would! What the hell was I thinking?

I hate this place. I don't want to die, but I can't let myself become one of those "things". I know what I have to do, even if my heart ain't in it. Dammit, back to the drawing board.

The stone pillars in this cavern are load-bearing. When my explosives detonate, the ceiling will collapse. I'll be buried under a ton of rubble. If I don't die in the explosion, at least I'll never get out.

This is going to work, dammit. I'm a demolitions expert. Why didn't I try this from the start?

entries.title: Minimum Security
entries.text:
Prisoners in Cell Block B are Minimum Security, but just because some of them were accountants, technicians, or whatever doesn't mean they aren't criminals. 

They deserve to be here, and you can't let them challenge your authority. If they say something isn't in the rules or isn't in the law, remind them that you ARE the law in this prison. Make an example of one of them if you need to. Otherwise, it's chaos.

entries.title: Building Maintenance
entries.text: This building is falling apart. I swear the prisoners are going to be able to just pull the bars off, the walls are so bad. Asked the Warden about our maintenance budget. He says there isn't one. That there's never been one. That I just need to "toughen up" if I want to keep working here.

entries.title: Prisoner Collars
entries.text:
Started fitting prisoners with the new collars. Prison walls not enough? We really got to blow their heads off if they go too far outside? Most of these prisoners aren't even here for capital crimes.

Tried to talk to the Warden, but he chewed me out. We've got a staff meeting coming up with all the guards once the collars are distributed. I'm bringing it up again then.

entries.title: Solitary
entries.text: Remember, solitary confinement means solitary. Don't talk to the prisoner. Don't even have a conversation near their cell. You only come around here when it's mealtime. You don't answer them when they try to talk to you. No contact, got it?

entries.title: Mad Dog Malone
entries.text: Under no circumstances should Mad Dog Malone be allowed out of solitary confinement. He's in there permanently. We let him out, he'll make nice with the other inmates, and soon enough this whole prison will be part of his gang.

items.name: Thomas Brennan's Announcement
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Warden Brennan
transcript.text: Attention, inmates. This is Warden Brennan speaking.

transcript.speaker: Warden Brennan
transcript.text: This morning, you were fitted with what the guards told you was a "Prisoner Collar."

transcript.speaker: Warden Brennan
transcript.text: This collar is an explosive device that will detonate if you attempt to leave Eastern Regional.

transcript.speaker: Warden Brennan
transcript.text: Now, before some of you panic and try to remove the collar, I feel it's important to advise you that doing so will also detonate the device.

transcript.speaker: Warden Brennan
transcript.text: Please don't think of these collars as a punishment, think of them as a benefit.

transcript.speaker: Warden Brennan
transcript.text: You will no longer be under scrutiny by guards, and you will no longer be forced to sit in your tiny cells as punishment for your crimes.

transcript.speaker: Warden Brennan
transcript.text: If you stay within the confines of this facility, you're free to roam about and do what you please.

transcript.speaker: Warden Brennan
transcript.text: However, if any of you choose to abuse this newly-found freedom, know that I will not hesitate to manually detonate your collar.

transcript.speaker: Warden Brennan
transcript.text: Provided we understand each other, I am certain that the rest of your sentence at Eastern Regional will pass quietly and comfortably.

transcript.speaker: Warden Brennan
transcript.text: Your cell doors are now unlocked. Enjoy your new life without bars, inmates.

entries.title: Warden Mainframe
entries.text:
Warden Brennan, with the installment of the new mainframe, your time at Eastern Regional is coming to an end. You will remain on staff to oversee the transition and until your retirement benefits kick in.

We really want to thank you both for your years of dedicated service and for your enthusiasm over the automation program. The future of correctional facilities is within reach, and you've been instrumental in making it possible.

entries.title: Transcript: D-Block Recording
entries.text:
Zander: So, wait. You're tellin' me everyone's gone? The guards, the cook staff, everyone?

Porter: Yeah. Well, not Warden Brennan. He's staying behind to keep an eye on us.

Zander: That's crazy. People are gonna kill each other in here.

Porter: Sure, if they want their heads to blow up. That's what these collars are for, remember? Besides, we've got those stupid robot guards now, so it ain't like we can do whatever the hell we want.

Zander: I don't know. Almost feels like the state's givin' up on us, lettin' us rot.

Porter: When did they ever care about us? This ain't new. This is just a way to keep the prison running and keep us in line.

Zander: Well, if Griffin and Carlo hadn't tried escapin', maybe we wouldn't be in this mess.

Porter: Probably not, but they're dead and we're not. Which reminds me, Ozzie is having a meeting tonight in the cafeteria. He claims he knows a guy that's good with electronics. Might be able to get these things off our necks. You in?

Zander: Hell no. You guys have fun, I plan on keepin' this head on my shoulders for the rest of my sentence.

entries.title: February 26, 2077
entries.text: Now Colton and Leland have passed on. The steel mill just keeps pumping poison out. I'm not sure what to do. What can I do? I can't get other work with my back being so bad and Arthur is kin.

entries.title: May 7,2077
entries.text: That cute Susy Jenkins died horrible with lumps growing inside her little body. I feel so bad for her folks. No one should have to bury a little child like that. I don't see that I have any choice. Arthur can't see past the dollar signs and doesn't give a crap about anything. People are dying.

entries.title: May 14, 2077
entries.text: I finally did it. I secretly told the news about what's happening here. The safety rules are ignored and kids are dying. It's not right.

entries.title: June 28, 2077
entries.text: Hoooooooo boy! I stirred up the hornet nest. There's protestors and reporters and all kind of people camping outside the steel works now. They're blocking the trucks and such. They're real riled up.

entries.title: July 2, 2077
entries.text: The soldiers came and cleared those folks out and posted guards with guns. Arthur was laughing about it today talking about those commie whiners getting what's coming to them. I guess I gotta try something else to make things right.

entries.title: August 14, 2077
entries.text: Got fired today and booted off the premises. Said they knew I was helping the protestors. Guess being kin didn't matter. Arthur didn't even talk to me himself. I guess I have to find another way.

entries.title: Mission Statement Notes
entries.text:
As part of our new federal government contract, we were given a grant to fund projects aimed at increasing steel yield from this plant. A secondary goal is to develop steel product specifically aimed at the military sector: steel for weaponry, vehicles, and the like.

Though the program is new for this facility, and our team is small, we already have projects underway, with more being researched every day.

entries.title: Project Phoenix
entries.text:
Project Phoenix /
----------------

Civilian Power Armor geared towards industrial applications is becoming all the rage in this region. (See, Garrahan Mining) 

Our goal is to create a suit of power armor able to be operated under intense heat conditions, allowing our workers to withstand greater temperatures and service machinery without needing to stop up the whole works. This could save us hours of productive work time.

Initial prototyping of the helmet is heading in the right direction, with the rest of the suit to follow.

entries.title: Project Adamantine
entries.text:
Project Adamantine /
-------------------

As part of the grant agreement, one of the military big-wigs included a provision that we need to focus efforts on creating a new steel alloy; something he kept referring to as "super steel."

It's ridiculous. We already have plenty of metal alloys stronger than steel: nickel, tungsten carbide, titanium, chromium, etc are all added to steel to produce stronger alloys.

But, he wanted something "that will blow them all away."

I'm not sure what to do about this one yet.

entries.title: Drink Choices
entries.text: I'm tired of only having Nuka-Cola available to buy in the break rooms, when there are a variety of other Nuka-Cola flavors.

entries.title: Smell
entries.text:
Something really stinks in the hallways and offices overlooking Sector Bravo. 

I asked my super to send maintenance to check the trash and desks around there  to see if anyone left their lunch to spoil. 

They tossed everyone's lunch just in case (sorry about that!), but there's still an incredible stench! Someone needs to do something about it!

entries.title: To Management
entries.text: I noticed someone suspicious hanging around near the vats, talking to himself. I couldn't make out his face or what he was saying, but when I approached, he ran off. When I brought it up to my manager, he told me not to worry about it, so I wanted to report it here just in case.

entries.title: Don't listen to Gerry!
entries.text: I was having an argument with Gerry about the Nuka-Cola in the break room. He wants to see more variety, but what's wrong with regular old Nuka-Cola? It's an American classic! If we start bringing in all that other shit, there'd be less room for the regular stuff, and once people drink all that, we'd have to resort to drinking Quantum or whatever!

entries.title: Robots
entries.text: I know the robots are here for our protection. But does anyone else feel like the government's just trying to keep tabs on us? I don't like it.

entries.title: Boogerman
entries.text: Someone keeps wiping their boogers all over the top of the urinals in all the men's rooms. I get that we're all big and tough steel workers, but do we have to live like animals? Someone do something about this!

entries.title: Thefts
entries.text: Someone stole the stack of magazines I was keeping in my locker. They were from my private collection, and I really don't want my wife finding out I had them. So if you can ask around, I just want to talk with whoever took them and explain.

entries.title: Nuka-Cola
entries.text:
Heads up, I saw the Nuka-Cola rep messing with the suggestion box on his way out. We should probably put a password or something on this thing.

While you're at it, can we get more water fountains? I'd like more to drink than sugary soda.

entries.title: Bonuses
entries.text:
We keep hearing the profits are way up, and we even got that fancy new government contract, but still haven't seen any of that extra dough hit our wallets. We haven't even hired any new guys, so what's the idea?

And this ain't a Union thing, just so you know. I just work hard and want a piece of the pie.

entries.title: Locker Room
entries.text: Can we get a separate locker room for women? I hate having to cover up all the windows in my truck and changing in there every day, and there's no way I'm undressing in front of those guys.

entries.title: Suggestion
entries.text: This thing's a joke. Only constructive feedback? You don't want suggestions, you just want people to feel like they're making a difference when you have no intention of ever doing anything about it. Give me a break.

entries.title: Incident Report: Fight
entries.text:
A fight broke out Monday afternoon between one of the welders, Mitch Douglas, and his foreman, Gil Freeman. The dispute was over a football game, where Mitch claims Gil had bet his truck if Mitch's team won, which it did. Gil then claimed that he was joking, and their argument escalated into a fight.

Light first aid was administered to both employees and both were placed on two weeks leave without pay.

entries.title: Incident Report: Injury
entries.text: Joey Cummings incurred major lacerations to the left arm, shoulder, neck, and face when loose clothing was caught in uncovered machinery while doing routine maintenance. He neglected to turn off the machine, or secure his clothing, leading to it getting caught in the rotors and pulling him in. An ambulence was called, and he is expected to make a full recovery. He'll be back to work pending doctor approval.

entries.title: Incident Report: LOL
entries.text:
We had our first Loss Of Life incident in 7 years. Today at approximately 9:30 AM, Steve Milner fell head-first into a smelting vat when an unsecured chain caught his leg and tripped him up. His wife and kids were notified via the local Mr. Messenger service.

As a result, I've ordered a full safety sweep, and I've sent for a new workplace safety film, which we'll play for all new and existing employees at a time and date TBD next week.

entries.title: Incident Report: Injury
entries.text:
Amelia Caravelli, a new hire, was subjected to a security scan by one of the government-issued Protectrons. Since HR had delayed getting her paperwork to the proper authorities, the Protectron mistook her for an unauthorized intruder. Normally, this wouldn't be a problem, because a foreman or supervisor would be able to override, but Amelia was working late in an effort to prove herself.

Luckily, a human security guard was alerted, and she was treated for moderate laser burns she sustained. Amelia was instructed on the importance of adhering to core working hours and given 2 days paid leave to recover.

items.contents:

-Paladin Taggerdy

items.contents:
Munch's Memoirs: A Whale of a Tale

Most of the kids here don't know the truth about whales. They used to be the largest, most feared land predators in North America. You always knew when they were coming because of the whale-quakes. They'd wake from hibernation out of the ground, and start burrowing their way to the surface.

Once on land, they were a force of pure destruction. A single whale could take down a whole building if it was still in their way. They had razor sharp fins to slice people in half, and gruesome baleen for teeth. If they sucked you in, that baleen would slice you up like a loaf of bread.

The kids found some old bones while digging out the Core. I told them they were lucky, not only because it was dead, but because that one was just a baby.

Long before we ever landed a man on the moon, USSA had already launched a top secret program to create the world's first space station: the Nova-Orbital-01. The space race was real, but the true mission was to gather information on the alien spies that infiltrated our planet.

The town of Flatwoods had already seen them. We knew they were out there, but we couldn't have a panic on our hands. We didn't know the alien motives, so the public could know nothing.

dirty swings
caps stuck in the frame rubbed glossy
    Each face dusty with the same mud
    caked on cake gone on

a cloud of flies the only reminder of nature
    reclaiming every tiny space

items.name: Journal: Hot Pursuit
items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
The world has gone to all hell, but miners still spend every waking hour hunting for riches in the jagged stone of Appalachia. Some things never change.

Every waking hour? Not quite accurate. For when the sun sets, their minds turn to other things -- chems, gambling, booze. I find myself entrapped in this den of debauchery. I'm not immune to its charms.

Besides, I came here for info. A lead on Little Rob, that notorious bandit who stalks the hills nearby, and I can tell I am close. Surly, the ringleader here, has said as much.

She insists I take chem after chem. This pill and that pill slide down my throat, lubricated by more whiskey than I knew existed. Untold doses of Buffout fill my veins. I'd say it's the price I pay for my art, but we all know I'd be lying. I enjoy it all too much to call it a toll.

I can't get enough of the stuff, and if they'll give it out for free, then why not partake? I get what I want and then some.

entries.text:
Sons of Dane Compound
----------------------------------------------------
Recon: Aldridge
Risk: Medium
Reward: Guns, Ammo

Aldridge said this place could still be worth looting. Meg mentioned it was an old Free States paramilitary compound that the Cutthroats never went after. Wonder why. Setting risk at medium until I can get more info.

entries.text:
Kanawha Nuka-Cola Plant
----------------------------------------------------
Recon: Axel
Risk: Low
Reward: Caps

Out of the way location. Axel said it doesn't look too overrun. If anything, there's gotta be a boatload of caps in there, right?

entries.title: --> Survival Training Center
entries.text:
Survival Training Center (Camp Venture)
----------------------------------------------------
Recon: Aldridge
Risk: High
Reward: Guns, Ammo, tech

Crazy Aldridge went into the Mire for this one, so Meg really thinks it's worth it. With both the Free States and Brotherhood having a presence here, there's bound to be some good shit we can use.

entries.title: --> West Tek
entries.text:
West Tek
----------------------------------------------------
Recon: Lev
Risk: High
Reward: Tech, Chems

Super Mutants aside, Lev thinks this place is a good hit for the chems alone. Meg's pretty sure the Cutthroats already ransacked the place, so I'll need more intel on it first.

entries.title: --> The Mire
entries.text:
The Mire
----------------------------------------------------
ALL OF IT.

I've lost three scouts to this place already, and it ain't looking good. We're lucky the Savage Divide acts as a natural barrier from that place. No one likes a swamp anyway.

entries.title: --> Grafton Steel
entries.text:
Grafton Steel
----------------------------------------------------
This place is overrun with Super Mutants. I got a few people keeping an eye out for any trouble just in case. Kiyomi's got that southern end of The Crater on lock down, so I ain't too worried about any surprise attacks... just attacks in general.

entries.title: --> Knife's Edge
entries.text:
Knife's Edge
----------------------------------------------------
Creed was saying he and Axel spotted some old camp just east of us. Looked like they were trying to be prepared, but failed horribly. He said that place looked like a breeding ground for some nasty critters. The big types.

entries.title: --> Toxic Waste Disposal
entries.text:
Toxic Waste Disposal
----------------------------------------------------
Aldridge said there's an old dump site for some toxic waste. Not that we'd have any interest there, but a pretty sizeable group of Scorched are hanging out there too. Meg's been eyeballing it as part of her "plan" to take them all out. I ain't sure that's the best idea.

items.name: Marcia's Diary

location.text: Found at The Crater War Room.

items.lead: A note lying in the world.
items.contents:
Everyone. Everyone is dead.

These assholes called the Brotherhood of Steel showed up and decided that we should fight back against the raiders who were taking our supplies. The Brotherhood gave everyone these weapons, but they got overwhelmed. The raiders took the weapons from us and slaughtered everyone. Including Mom.

If the Brotherhood had never shown up, everyone would still be alive. If we didn't try to fight back, the raiders would have taken what they wanted and left, just like they always have.

Their blood is on the Brotherhood's hands.

entries.title: Extended Hours
entries.text:
To: All Employees
Subj: Extended Hours

For the first time in our park's history we will be extending our hours into October! The weather has been so mild this year that we have an opportunity to welcome more visitors before our winter shut down and maintenance.  During October we plan to be open:

Monday thru Friday - Noon to 4 p.m.
Saturday & Sunday - 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.

We will close as needed should the weather turn unpleasant.

- Management

entries.title: October Birthdays
entries.text:
To: All Employees
Subj: Birthday Parties

The following birthday parties will be hosted in the Splish Splash area for the month of October:
>> October 2 - Johnson family and friends celebrating the 8th birthday of Stacie Johnson
>> October 13 - Williams & Llewelyn families celebrating the 3rd birthday of Blanche Williams
>> October 17 - Davies family and friends celebrating the 7th birthday of Nate Davies.

All available staff members will be gathered to sing Happy Birthday to the kids.

- Management

entries.title: Arrivals
entries.text:
To: All Employees
Subj: Shift Arrival

Staff members will no longer be permitted on the premises more than an hour prior to a scheduled shift and they must depart the premises within an hour after the end of their work day. Unfortunately, this policy had to be put in place because some employees were loitering after work or arriving early to enjoy rides without paying even a discounted staff admission fee. This behavior is selfish and will not be tolerated.

- Management

entries.title: Holotape Reviews
entries.text:
To: All Employees
Subj: Holotapes

All employees who are assisting in the review should report to the underground section of the staff area where the past month's holotapes are stored. Check in with the security supervisor on duty there so your time is recorded correctly. Your help is greatly appreciated.

- Management

entries.title: Counterfeit Bills
entries.text:
Notice to all employees:
In the month of September a total of 5 counterfeit bills were passed to unwary staff members with the total loss amounting to $47. This was our worst month in the history of the park! Security staff will conduct training immediately to help employees identify these fakes. It is in your best interest to pay attention as any further losses due to your inattention will be taken out of your pay.

entries.title: Trespassing
entries.text:
Notice to all employees:
In the early morning hours on October 15th, a section of our park fence was scaled by an intruder. This individual attempted to break into the storerooms in the underground employee restricted area but was disturbed in the act of prying the door open by our alert watchman. This criminal ran off and managed to escape his just punishment.

This doesn't seem to be the local kids because commie propaganda denouncing the war effort was dropped as the intruder fled. The police have been alerted to the possibility of a plot and are on the lookout. If you have any information to provide contact management immediately!

entries.title: Kidnapping
entries.text:
Notice to all employees:
Everyone has heard about the missing child, Freddy, who may have been kidnapped from our very own water park as part of some anti-war protest. Management and our security staff are working closely with the Grafton police to find the child. Any employee that is able to come in to help review security holotapes will be paid overtime for the hours they spend.

entries.title: October 19
entries.text:
Day shift notes - 
Looked at Slither Slide and Kiddie Slide for 12 hours.

Found a tape that is probably the kid getting nabbed at the Slither. I think the kid knew the guy. Put it in the sec office safe till the feds or whoever can come get it. - Pete

entries.title: October 22
entries.text:
This is getting tiring.
Six hours of gator mouth and another four of the picnic tables up top. No luck - Pete

entries.title: October 23
entries.text: Three hours of concessions. Got a guy acting real weird about a package, might be the same guy as that slide tape. Setting it aside, I'll bring it to the office end of shift. - Tom

Arthur, my dearest.

I am both frightened and excited that we will soon be parents. I am so glad you've agreed to let Otis work with you at the mill. I know he irritates you but he's my only brother and I love him.

- Scoutmaster James A. Johnson

Jeff Perry

entries.title: Vault Tec - Project Safehouse
entries.text:
Mr. Wood,

To answer your questions:

1. Yes, there is room for both you and your son
2. Yes, your war efforts are greatly appreciated
3. Yes, you can arrange for your son to be delivered to a safe location in the event of war since you will likely be separated from him. If he is at either location you specified: his home, his school, we will be able to assist.
4. No, his nanny will not be able to join him

Regards,
Vault-Tec

entries.title: Safety Data
entries.text:
Mr. Wood,

I'm afraid the worker safety numbers this past quarter have increased drastically over the previous quarter. This might look pretty bad if released to the regulatory board. Even with our government preferred status Grafton Steel would take a lot of heat. Maybe we can adjust the format of the report?

This is another argument for automated workers though. Repair costs are a lot cheaper than lawsuits.

What do you think?
Stacie

entries.title: Morale
entries.text:
Mr. Wood,

Worker morale has been plummeting. I started asking around and I think Otis Pike is bad-mouthing the company. With your permission, I will arrange for his activities to be watched more closely.

Respectfully,
Stacie

entries.title: Termination
entries.text:
Mr. Wood,

I've terminated the problem employee and reported his commie leanings to the authorities as you requested. Under the Wartime Workers Act he could hang for treason if you want to press this issue. Please advise?

Stacie

entries.title: Production
entries.text:
Mr. Wood,

Our numbers are dropping fast. I think the workers are intentionally damaging automated help. I'm not sure they're going to be the best solution in these turbulent times.

Can you investigate whether conscription is an option while we wait for the delivery of more automated workers?

Regards,
Stacie

items.name: Battle of Huntersville Speech
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: Civilization.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: The Brotherhood and Responders together have paid a high price to make that word mean something in Appalachia.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: Despite all the changes, farmers have worked the land, people have learned new skills, and we've built a new world.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: And the Super Mutants threaten all of that.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: I'm a soldier, a Paladin, and I tell you that this is our moment.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: We will never be stronger, and the Super Mutant's never weaker.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: If you are thinking in the heat of battle to run, live to fight another day, know this.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: There is no other day. We win here, now, Responders and Brotherhood together... or we will die.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: So look to your left, look to your right. Promise to give your all to protect them, and they will protect you.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: Make no mistake, this will be the toughest fight of our lives.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: But we will win, because we're fighting for something. For each other, for our children, for civilization.

transcript.speaker: Elizabeth Taggerdy
transcript.text: Now let's show these Muties what we're made of.

items.name: Cooper Lu's journal
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Cooper Lu
transcript.text: The holotape machine is on it's last legs, so I'm recording this for whoever comes along that might find a working one.

transcript.speaker: Cooper Lu
transcript.text: My name is Cooper Lu. I'm the last survivor of Clarksburg. After everything fell apart, a lot of them left for Morgantown.

transcript.speaker: Cooper Lu
transcript.text: There was some arguing over who got the guns from the shooting range, but a few warning shots settled that.

transcript.speaker: Cooper Lu
transcript.text: A while later a bunch of us got sick when the water turned funny colors. It took them a long time to die.

transcript.speaker: Cooper Lu
transcript.text: That just left me, Jill and Ande. Some god damn mutated bear thing got them. Now it's just me.

transcript.speaker: Cooper Lu
transcript.text: I'm going to head out east and see if I can find people. Anyone listening to this should do the same. Goodbye, probably forever.

items.name: Darius Angler's Manifesto, part 2
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: They killed my brother! Those bastards at the Grafton Steel Mill killed Billy.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: Mandatory overtime they called it. He should never have been on those catwalks.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: I can't even bury him. When you fall into a vat of molten steel there's nothing left of you.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: I'll get them for this. I'll show those bastards.

items.name: Darius Angler's Manifesto, part 3
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: I've uncovered a conspiracy between the government and Grafton Steel. Kickbacks, wink and nod inspections, bribes, you name it.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: There's no telling how big this is. I think they bugged my house, so I've moved to a cabin in the woods where nobody can find me.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: Yesterday I had to shoot a woman. She claimed she was just hiking, but I know she was an agent sent to spy on me.

items.name: Darius Angler's Manifesto, part 4
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: I've booby trapped my cabin. They're attaching listening devices to the raccoons to spy on me.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: But I'm too smart for them. They can't get past my traps.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: I saw a fox look funny at me today. They might be using them too. If I see another one come around, that will prove it.

items.name: Darius Angler's Manifesto, part 6
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: The air raid sirens. The ground shaking. It's Billy. He's telling me it's time. Everyone is thinking about the bombs. They won't notice me.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: All I have to do is sneak in to Grafton Steel and use my secret formula. Then their smoke stacks will begin spewing toxic dust all over the valley.

transcript.speaker: Darius Angler
transcript.text: Then they'll be sorry they hurt Billy. They'll be sorry and dead.

items.name: First Day of Command
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: So I got my own command now. Bet you never thought that would happen, right?

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: But with all the new blood Sarge is training... I mean Knight. Senior Knight.

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: Met up with a representative of the Responders.

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: I told him our mission: to escort trade caravans, keep the freaks from the Savage Divide away from civilization, and maybe get the Dam operational again.

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: She was so grateful, it was almost embarrassing.

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: Day one complete and so far so good.

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: But I miss you. And the hot shower! But mostly you.

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: The old rules about fraternization... I don't know if they apply in the Brotherhood.

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: Maybe we can just come clean and tell Paladin Taggerdy about us?

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: I know you'd like kids one day, too, and we're not getting any younger.

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: Promise you'll think about it.

transcript.speaker: Johnny Moreno
transcript.text: Love you!

items.name: George Smith's memo
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: George N. Smith
transcript.text: This is Director George N. Smith recording what may be my final memo.

transcript.speaker: George N. Smith
transcript.text: The earthquakes that followed the nukes cracked the dam somewhere.

transcript.speaker: George N. Smith
transcript.text: I can't see the rupture, but the lake level has dropped dramatically.

transcript.speaker: George N. Smith
transcript.text: The Pioneer Scout Camp got it worse though. Some sort of underground sink hole dropped most of it to below the normal lake water level.

transcript.speaker: George N. Smith
transcript.text: Ironically it's now at the new beach front level. If the reservoir were full, it would be totally submerged.

transcript.speaker: George N. Smith
transcript.text: I'm heading out now to see if anyone out there needs help. I don't know what I'll find. This is George N. Smith signing off.

items.name: Homecoming
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.text: Appalachia. I thought it was going to be in the rear view forever. Coming back... is weird.
The Gourmands freaks are all gone. Even those gun-toting maniac Cutthroats.
Leaving was humiliating, but Meg called it. And now she'll neeeever let us forget it.

items.name: Isabel Smith-Waltz's journal
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Isabel Smith-Waltz
transcript.text: It's my first day here. Oh, this is Isabel Smith-Waltz. Can't forget introductions.

transcript.speaker: Isabel Smith-Waltz
transcript.text: The rangers are all so friendly, but this place is kind of weird.

transcript.speaker: Isabel Smith-Waltz
transcript.text: So this fort was supposed to be a rebuilt frontier fort, but the railroad went through the place where it really used to be, so they had to put it here.

transcript.speaker: Isabel Smith-Waltz
transcript.text: Then they found out the guy who wrote the book that described the fort made most of it up. Crazy, right?

transcript.speaker: Isabel Smith-Waltz
transcript.text: So it doesn't even look like the real one. We call it a 'representational frontier fort.'

transcript.speaker: Isabel Smith-Waltz
transcript.text: Now they want to start running civil war battle recreations here. But that never happened either. But they say it will bring in lots of money.

transcript.speaker: Isabel Smith-Waltz
transcript.text: Some people just to appreciate real history.

items.name: James Waltz's notes
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: James Waltz
transcript.text: Some days I wish I had never inherited Hemlock Holes.

transcript.speaker: James Waltz
transcript.text: Who names a golf course after a poison? My father, that's who.

transcript.speaker: James Waltz
transcript.text: And, to top it all off, we're stuck out here in the ass-end of the country.

transcript.speaker: James Waltz
transcript.text: I've bought one of those fancy Mr. Handy chefs. Maybe some community cookouts will drum up more business.

items.name: John Bunton's Holotape
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: John Bunton
transcript.text: Damn it, is this thing... Okay. Okay, it's recording. Ol' JB here. And you would not believe what I'm seein' right now!

transcript.speaker: John Bunton
transcript.text: I'm sittin' here drivin' this truck, and what do I see ahead, but a sky full of... well there's these streaks of light like nothin' I ever seen.

transcript.speaker: John Bunton
transcript.text: Boy howdy, it's majestic. Like shootin' stars in the early mornin' light, only I ain't never seen 'em in the mornin' like this.

transcript.speaker: John Bunton
transcript.text: It's like a rocket streakin' through the blue sky, or like a... oh... oh shit. It's a nuclear...

transcript.speaker: John Bunton
transcript.text: <Faint nuclear explosion in the distance>

transcript.speaker: John Bunton
transcript.text: Aw shit, it exploded. I was starin' right at it, and I... I can't see! I... I'm going to...

transcript.speaker: John Bunton
transcript.text: <Sound of a truck running off the road, metal screeching, and glass breaking>

transcript.speaker: John Bunton
transcript.text: <Nuclear blast shockwave hitting>

transcript.speaker: John Bunton
transcript.text: <Sound of something large pounding on the metal walls of the truck's trailer and ripping the door off the back>

items.name: Mayor Mudge's private memo
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Richard Mudge
transcript.text: Just got back from a town council meeting. Bunch of pansies. No vision. No brains. No balls.

transcript.speaker: Richard Mudge
transcript.text: I'm going to drag the lot of them into the 22nd century if it's the last thing I do.

transcript.speaker: Richard Mudge
transcript.text: Since I have dirt on most of those yellow belly piss ants, they won't have much of a choice.

transcript.speaker: Richard Mudge
transcript.text: Tourism! That's what this place needs. Bunch of wide-eyed marks wandering around spending their cash on shit they don't need.

transcript.speaker: Richard Mudge
transcript.text: Grafton steel is the past. Water parks and shooting ranges are the future.

transcript.speaker: Richard Mudge
transcript.text: But I have to be careful. Grafton Steel is a big campaign contributor. Can't let them think I don't have their backs.

transcript.speaker: Richard Mudge
transcript.text: At least not until I stab them there.

items.name: Meg Sucks
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.text: She talks such a big game, but what do we actually do?
We pick away at stragglers. We try not to rock the boat.
These settlers are on my land. Hell, there's a family living in my old house
Lev. Lev's the solution. Meg's gotta be retired. One way or the other.

items.name: Repair Plan
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Donna Mason
transcript.text: I dunno what all they put in the furnace, but it's gaumed it up but good.

transcript.speaker: Donna Mason
transcript.text: Wouldn't have been so bad if ya'll had just shut damned thing down for a few weeks and cleaned out the blast.

transcript.speaker: Donna Mason
transcript.text: But at this point? Whatever it is, at this point it's fused with every damned part from the Furnace to the Smelter and the Mills.

transcript.speaker: Supervisor Fortney
transcript.text: Look Mason, I don't need to hear it. Can you keep it running or not?

transcript.speaker: Donna Mason
transcript.text: Ain't gonna be easy. Whatever's going on chemically, it's pretty toxic and corrosive at that.

transcript.speaker: Donna Mason
transcript.text: You're gonna have to keep making near constant repairs. I can mark the areas, but that's not gonna stop the ash...

transcript.speaker: Supervisor Fortney
transcript.text: Foreman doesn't give a damn about the ash. The workers brought it on themselves, now they get to live with it.

transcript.speaker: Supervisor Fortney
transcript.text: Besides, the bots don't give a damn. All the more reason to continue the workforce change over.

transcript.speaker: Donna Mason
transcript.text: So that's it then? Just... keep replacing bots and machinery. Let the plant destroy the valley and break up the strikers?

transcript.speaker: Supervisor Fortney
transcript.text: If you've got a problem with that, we can cancel payment.

transcript.speaker: Donna Mason
transcript.text: It's just...

transcript.speaker: Donna Mason
transcript.text: Aw, shit. Just get me in the van and get me out of here before anyone sees me.

transcript.speaker: Supervisor Fortney
transcript.text: Pleasure doing business with you. We'll recommend you to our friends.

transcript.speaker: Donna Mason
transcript.text: Don't. Don't ever contact me again after this.

transcript.speaker: Donna Mason
transcript.text: And erase my name off that holotape. I went over the needed repairs, that's enough.

transcript.speaker: Supervisor Fortney
transcript.text: Fine.

items.name: The Addington's Dangerous Game
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Carl Addington
transcript.text: Well, another hunting season comes to a close. I guess we should start packing up the lodge.

transcript.speaker: Westley Addington
transcript.text: Yes, I suppose we should.

transcript.speaker: Carl Addington
transcript.text: What's the problem? This was a great season.

transcript.speaker: Westley Addington
transcript.text: I know. It's just, well, it's getting quite boring. We hunt the same thing, every year.

transcript.speaker: Carl Addington
transcript.text: Oh my god, then what do you want? If you have something to say, then spit it out already!

transcript.speaker: Westley Addington
transcript.text: All right. Before you judge, hear me out.

transcript.speaker: Westley Addington
transcript.text: What if we hunted something new? Something that was a real challenge for a change. Something that could fight back.

transcript.speaker: Westley Addington
transcript.text: We circulate an advertisement offering a free weekend at the lodge. People will have no idea what they're really getting into. It's perfect!

transcript.speaker: Carl Addington
transcript.text: Wait. Are you talking about hunting... humans?

transcript.speaker: Westley Addington
transcript.text: Oh, don't act so surprised. You know it makes sense. I can see it on your face.

transcript.speaker: Carl Addington
transcript.text: Do you really think we can get away with it?

transcript.speaker: Westley Addington
transcript.text: With our wealth, dear brother, we can get away with anything.

items.name: The Foundation Plan
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Raider
transcript.text: So C backed out. I swear, I'm losing more people than recruiting.

transcript.speaker: Raider
transcript.text: If we could just crack Foundation, we'd be rich. And we'd own Appalachia.

transcript.speaker: Raider
transcript.text: But the damned walls, and they've got numbers, too.

transcript.speaker: Raider
transcript.text: I'd go with explosives but Lou won't have anything to do with my "cockamamey plan."

transcript.speaker: Raider
transcript.text: *sigh* I could try the Blood Eagles...? Who am I kidding, they'd just lynch me. Damned Foundation.
